label: Fetch to Storage
description: Download a file from a URL straight into storage and emit a file reference. The bytes stream directly into storage (never buffered whole), so it handles large files. Wire `file` into MediaDisplay, DownloadLink, KeepFile, or any node that takes a stored file. To fetch a thing ONCE per project however many runs ask for it, set `scope` to `project` and give it an `identity` (a label for the source, such as `docs:invoice-42`): a second fetch of the same identity answers the file already stored and downloads nothing. This node downloads; for a file the run already holds in storage (an upload, a generated image) that later runs need to read, use KeepFile with `scope: project` instead.

inputs.name: url
inputs.description: URL of the file to fetch.

inputs.name: filename
inputs.description: Override the stored filename. Defaults to the URL's last path segment.

inputs.name: scope
inputs.label: Store in
inputs.description: `execution`: the file belongs to this run, and only this run can read it. `project`: it belongs to the project, and every later run can read it.

inputs.name: ttl_days
inputs.label: Keep for (days, 0 = forever)
inputs.description: How long the file lives once nobody touches it: any access (read, download, presign) resets the clock, and 0 means never expire. Empty means an execution file is swept shortly after its run ends, and a project file lives until deleted.

inputs.name: identity
inputs.label: Identity
inputs.description: What the file is a copy of, as a stable label (`<source>:<id>`). A fetch whose identity is already stored in the chosen scope answers that file and downloads nothing, so the same document asked for by many runs is one file. Leave empty for a file that is its own thing.

outputs.name: filename
outputs.description: The name the file is stored under.
